sections.h2: How quickly can a Converse house be sold?
sections.html:
A cash sale is the fastest of the three common routes, and it suits a house that needs work or a seller with a firm deadline. Converse owners can also list with an agent or sell privately.

Converse sits in northeastern Bexar County, about thirteen miles from downtown San Antonio according to the Texas State Historical Association. Sellers range from long-time family owners to heirs and owners facing a tax bill or a job move.

  • Cash buyer: an as-is price, a closing date you set and no showings.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, but showings, buyer loans and repair requests add weeks.
  • Sale of an inherited house: first confirm who has authority to sign the deed.
  • Sale with taxes due: the payoff comes out of proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What do the QuickFacts numbers show about Converse?
sections.html:
Converse is young and growing, and about three in four homes have an owner living in them. The table lists figures from the QuickFacts page.

Households average 2.86 people, and 27.7% of residents are under 18, so family-sized houses are the typical product. Median rent of $1,693 is a useful figure when a buyer plans to rent the house out.

sections.h2: How did Converse turn from farm town to suburb?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas says the town was named for a Major Converse, chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, who bought the townsite tract in 1877. A post office opened in 1878.

The entry describes the community as originally settled by German farmers and says it reportedly had the oldest 4-H Club in Texas by 1990. A singing society, the Salatrillo Liederkranz, was active for many years. By 1946 the population was 175, and by 1965 there were twenty-two businesses and 900 residents.

Growth then arrived quickly. The population was 8,887 in 1990 and 11,508 in 2000, and the Census estimate for 2025 is 32,481. For a seller, that history means houses of very different ages: older homes near the original roads and newer subdivisions built since the 1990s.

sections.h2: What else do the Census figures say about Converse residents?
sections.html:
QuickFacts counts 10,288 households and gives the city 8.46 square miles of land, up from 6.98 in 2010. The 2020 density was 3,247.3 people per square mile, tighter than the other cities in this series, and the population has climbed from 18,198 in 2010 to 27,466 in 2020.

  • Veterans: 3,352 residents.
  • Age: 6.3% under 5 and 11.1% aged 65 or older.
  • Schooling: 94.1% of adults over 25 hold a diploma, and 33.9% hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Commute: 26.8 minutes on average.
  • Broadband: 95.0% of households.
  • 2022 retail sales: $264,605 thousand, or $8,936 per person.
  • Persons in poverty: 11.6%, with 14.3% of those under 65 lacking health insurance.

Retail sales per person are well below those of larger shopping centers nearby, which suggests Converse residents shop and work largely in other parts of the San Antonio area. A seller can emphasize the commute and the family-size floor plans.

sections.h2: When are Bexar County property taxes due for a Converse house?
sections.html:
The Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector says taxes are due in October and must be paid by January 31, with the payment postmarked by that date to be timely. Taxes are delinquent on February 1.

Past-due taxes are surrendered for collection on July 1 and carry an additional 15 or 20 percent collection fee, according to the county page. For business property, jurisdictions may send accounts for collection from April 1.

  • Bexar Appraisal District sets values, grants exemptions and records changes of ownership or address.
  • The tax office sends bills and takes payments; its FAQ lists a duplicate statement option if yours does not arrive.
  • A missing bill does not cancel the tax, penalty, interest or lien.

sections.h2: What payment plans does Bexar County offer Converse owners?
sections.html:
The county lists a half-payment option, a four-payment plan and a ten-month plan. Which one you can use depends on your exemptions.

  • Half-payment: pay at least half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the next year.
  • Four-payment plan for homestead owners who are 65 or older or disabled: January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.
  • Ten-month plan: the county says its office is the only one in Texas with this plan, open to a residence homestead with a disabled, over 65 or disabled veteran exemption, or a surviving spouse 55 or older of those groups, with payments from October through July.

The ten-month plan can still be joined in November with 20 percent down. The county also says early-payment discounts ended by a 2003 commissioners court order.

sections.h2: Can a senior or military owner defer taxes in Converse?
sections.html:
Yes, both deferrals exist. An owner 65 or older or disabled can file a deferral affidavit with Bexar Appraisal District to postpone taxes on the homestead, with interest at five percent a year. If the owner moves away or stops owning the house, the county says the past taxes and deferred interest become due on the 181st day.

Active-duty service members out of state during a declared war or emergency may defer under Property Tax Code section 31.02(b). The county asks for form 50-305 and military orders, and taxes may be paid without penalty up to 60 days after the earliest of listed events such as discharge or return to Texas for more than 10 days. If you have a deferral, ask the tax office for a payoff before you list.

sections.h2: How do I find out what is owed on a Converse house?
sections.html:
Ask for a tax certificate. The county says the fee is $10.00 per certificate, payment is required first, and it shows the status of taxes including penalties and interest if they are delinquent.

The owner on January 1 of the tax year is personally liable even if the house was sold during the year, and the lien follows the property. For that reason buyers and title companies ask for the certificate before closing, and sellers should pull it early to avoid surprises at the table.

sections.h2: What exemptions help a Converse buyer or seller?
sections.html:
The county lists the general residence homestead, a disabled exemption, a 100 percent disabled veteran exemption and an over-65 exemption. The state sets a $140,000 school district homestead exemption according to the Comptroller, plus $60,000 for age 65 or older or disabled.

For a buyer who closes after January 1, the Comptroller says the exemption can start immediately when the previous owner had none. Applications for the tax year go to the appraisal district, which the county says must be filed before May 1.

sections.h2: What if a Converse house is inherited or has liens?
sections.html:
Establish title first. The State Law Library says a will should be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit is for estates of $75,000 or less excluding homestead, with all heirs agreeing and the court approving. A transfer on death deed passes the house outside probate if it was recorded before the owner's death.

If taxes were sold at a tax sale, a Texas Supreme Court opinion cited by the Comptroller notes that homestead owners can redeem within two years of the purchaser's deed filing, at a premium that rises from 25 to 50 percent. Surplus from a tax foreclosure sale can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

faqs.a: Converse is in northeastern Bexar County, about thirteen miles northeast of downtown San Antonio, on Farm Road 1976 according to the Texas State Historical Association.

faqs.q: Does Bexar County have a ten-month tax payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says it is the only county in Texas with one, for homesteads with an over-65, disabled or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

faqs.q: What is a Bexar County tax certificate?
faqs.a: It is a document showing the status of taxes on a property, with penalties and interest if delinquent. The county charges $10.00 per certificate and wants payment first.

faqs.q: Who sets property values for a Converse home?
faqs.a: Bexar Appraisal District identifies the property, values it and decides exemptions. The tax office bills and collects. Call the appraisal district for exemptions and the tax office for statements.

faqs.q: Do I still owe taxes if I sold my Converse house during the year?
faqs.a: The county says the owner on January 1 is personally liable even after selling, and the lien follows the property, so closing papers should settle the year's tax.
